en.summary: PowerShell ran with an execution policy bypass, a hidden window and an encoded command that starts with Start-Job -ScriptBlock {(saps ("p. This pattern is attributed to MERCURY and most likely means malicious background execution.
en.what_it_detects: Windows process creation events whose CommandLine contains both '-exec bypass -w 1 -enc' and the Base64 (UTF-16LE) fragment of 'Start-Job -ScriptBlock {(saps ("p'. That decodes to a background job that launches a process with Start-Process.
en.why_it_matters: According to the Microsoft reference, MERCURY (G0069) used this pattern after exploiting Log4j 2 on unpatched systems. It maps to T1059.001 (PowerShell): code execution that hides in background jobs.
triage_steps: Decode the value after -enc in CommandLine (Base64, UTF-16LE) and note which process saps starts and with which arguments.
Check ParentImage. A java.exe, web service or application server parent points to remote exploitation such as Log4j.
Identify the user and host. Confirm whether that account normally runs PowerShell.
Review child and grandchild processes of the powershell.exe on the same host within +/- 15 minutes.
Look for outbound connections, downloads and new files in the same time window.
Search other endpoints for the same Base64 fragment or CommandLine to scope the activity.
Review the exposed application's logs and earlier alerts about Log4j exploitation for this host.
false_positives: The rule lists no known false positives (Unknown).
Red team or adversary emulation exercises that replay MERCURY tradecraft.
Authorized detection tests, such as Atomic Red Team or rule validation in a lab.
response_steps: Confirm the activity is malicious from the decoded payload and the parent process before you act.
Isolate the endpoint with the EDR and preserve memory and PowerShell logs (event 4104).
Kill the malicious processes and jobs, then remove the artifacts and persistence you identified.
Patch Log4j 2 and the affected software, and rotate credentials that were used on the host.
Restore the system from a trusted baseline and monitor for related indicators coming back.
en.severity_rationale: High fits because this exact combination of flags and payload is specific to the APT activity and has almost no legitimate use.
